title: [Test] Use larger client ports range for tests running on Windows

timeline.message:
[Test] Use larger client ports range for tests running on Windows

This PR increases client's port ranges for tests which are executed
on Windows in order to avoid failures due to some port ranges being
excluded from use. The larger ports range (300) is chosen based on
the observation where a random consecutive range of 200 ports is excluded.

Closes #102349
timeline.author: Slobodan Adamovic

timeline.body:
This PR increases client's port ranges for tests which are executed 
on Windows in order to avoid failures due to some port ranges being 
excluded from use. The larger ports range (300) is chosen based on 
the observation where a random consecutive range of 200 ports can 
be excluded on Windows test workers.

Closes #102349

timeline.author: Slobodan Adamovic

timeline.body:
The `elasticsearch-ci/part-2-fips` failure is unrelated and already tracked here: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/90549

@elasticmachine run elasticsearch-ci/part-2-fips
300 seem like a large bump from 10. Why is this one different than the other tests? Should it be `300 : 100` here too?

reply.body:
10 was a value chosen initially in this test and it seems that it was sufficient enough for this test on all other operating systems except on Windows. I kept the initial values in all tests and only bumped the range on Windows.

`randomPortRange = Strings.format("%s-%s", randomPort, randomPort + 10)`
